mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where both GDPC1 and HOUST meet the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and corporate earnings momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when INDPRO meets the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 100k signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes under these labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4% indicates disinflation despite restrictive policy, which typically signals easing financial conditions and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when both CPIAUCSL < 2% and FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly real savings rate (RSAFS/GDPC1) persistently above 7% for four consecutive months indicates households are saving a larger share of income, reducing consumption and investment demand, which translates to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not underperform the risk-free rate by at least 2% in 60-day periods following four months of RSAFS/GDPC1 > 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) decline of more than 200k while unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by at least 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month - 200000 AND UNRATE > previous month + 0.3
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes meeting both PAYEMS and UNRATE thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings and profit expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically greater than zero (t-test p > 0.10) during any 6-month window where INDPRO > 1% monthly.
